dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: What breathing symptoms have you noticed recently?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: I have been wheezing at night for the last three nights, and sometimes my chest feels tight.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: Have you needed your inhaler more often?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I have used my salbutamol inhaler several times, especially before going to sleep.

dialogue.speaker: child
dialogue.text: You have been coughing at night too. I can hear you from my room.

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: Yes, that is true. The cough is worse during the night.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: Have you had fever or signs of a cold?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: No fever. I have not really felt sick otherwise.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: Does your inhaler completely relieve the wheezing?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: It helps for a while, but the wheezing returns later.

dialogue.speaker: child
dialogue.text: Last night you woke up twice because you were coughing.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: That is useful to know. We may need to review your asthma treatment and your current control.
